def find_possible_message(t: str) -> str:
    n = len(t)
    
    for i in range(1, n):
        s1 = t[:i]
        s2 = t[i:]
        
        # Check if s2 starts with a suffix of s1
        if s2.startswith(s1[-1:]):
            # Try all possible overlaps of length 1 to len(s1)
            for overlap_len in range(1, len(s1)):
                if s1.endswith(s2[:overlap_len]):
                    return "YES\n" + s1
    
    return "NO"

# Reading input and outputting result
import sys
input = sys.stdin.read
t = input().strip()
print(find_possible_message(t))

def can_have_error(t):
    n = len(t)
    
    # Try all possible lengths of the first message
    for i in range(1, n):
        s1 = t[:i]
        s2 = t[i:]
        
        # Check if s2 starts with a suffix of s1
        if s2.startswith(s1[-1]):
            j = 1
            # Find the longest common suffix/prefix
            while j < len(s1) and s1[-(j+1)] == s2[j]:
                j += 1
            
            # If there is a common suffix/prefix of at least one character
            if j > 0:
                merged = s1 + s2[j:]
                if merged == t:
                    return "YES\n" + s1

    # If no error possible
    return "NO\n"

def can_have_error(t):
    n = len(t)
    
    # Iterate over all possible start points of the first message
    for i in range(1, n):
        first_message = t[:i]
        second_message = t[i:]
        
        # Check if there's any valid overlap between the end of the first
        # and the start of the second message
        for j in range(1, len(first_message) + 1):
            if first_message[-j:] == second_message[:j]:
                return "YES\n" + first_message
    
    return "NO"
